draft.title: Modelling non-linear data
card: Some curved data fit a rule y = kx^n, where n is a power such as 2, 3 or 1/2. The constant k sets the size of y.
Once you pick the power n, plot y against x^n. If the points lie on a straight line through the origin, the rule fits.
The gradient of that line is k. Find it as y ÷ x^n for any point on the line.
Example: x = 2 and y = 24 fit y = kx³. Then x³ = 8, so k = 24 ÷ 8 = 3 and the rule is y = 3x³.
draft.remember: Plot y against x^n. The gradient of the straight line is k.

a.q: Data fit y = kx². The point x = 3, y = 45 lies on the curve. What is k?
a.why: x² = 9, so k = 45 ÷ 9 = 5. The value 15 comes from dividing by x instead of x².

b.q: The area of a circular garden bed is modelled as A = kr². When r = 2 m, A = 12.56 m². Which is the area when r = 5 m?
b.why: k = 12.56 ÷ 4 = 3.14. Then A = 3.14 × 25 = 78.5. The value 31.4 comes from scaling the area by 5 ÷ 2 instead of squaring the radius ratio.

final.title: Modelling non-linear data
card: Some curved data fit a rule \(y = kx^{n}\), where \(n\) is a power such as 2, 3 or \(\frac{1}{2}\). The constant \(k\) sets the size of \(y\).
Once you pick the power \(n\), plot \(y\) against \(x^{n}\). If the points lie on a straight line through the origin, the rule fits.
The gradient of that line is \(k\). Find it as \(y \div x^{n}\) for any point on the line.
Example: \(x = 2\) and \(y = 24\) fit \(y = kx^{3}\). Then \(x^{3} = 8\), so \(k = 24 \div 8 = 3\) and the rule is \(y = 3x^{3}\).
final.remember: Plot \(y\) against \(x^{n}\). The gradient of the straight line is \(k\).

a.q: Data fit \(y = kx^{2}\). The point \(x = 3\), \(y = 45\) lies on the curve. What is \(k\)?
a.why: \(x^{2} = 9\), so \(k = 45 \div 9 = 5\). The value 15 comes from dividing by \(x\) instead of \(x^{2}\).

b.q: The area of a circular garden bed is modelled as \(A = kr^{2}\). When \(r = 2\) m, \(A = 12.56\text{ m}^{2}\). Which is the area when \(r = 5\) m?
b.why: \(k = 12.56 \div 4 = 3.14\). Then \(A = 3.14 \times 25 = 78.5\). The value 31.4 comes from scaling the area by \(5 \div 2\) instead of squaring the radius ratio.
